plainTranslation:
This connection can make it hard to tell love from longing.

At first, being seen by this person may feel beautiful. The Neptune person may look at the Venus person and sense something lovely, rare, or full of promise. The Venus person may feel deeply moved by that gaze, as though someone has finally noticed the most beautiful part of them.

But the square makes the image unstable.

The Venus person may begin shaping themselves around what the Neptune person wants to see. The Neptune person may avoid anything that complicates the fantasy. Both people may sense that something is unclear, but the feeling between them can make honesty strangely difficult. No one wants to break the spell.

This is where the relationship can become heavy.

One person may take on the job of staying lovely, forgiving, inspiring, or easy to adore. The other may settle into the dream and resist seeing what is real. It can feel romantic at first. Eventually it can become exhausting. You may realize that the relationship has been protecting an image instead of getting to know the people inside it.

There may not be any intentional deception here. More often, both of you are relating to an idea of each other instead of the actual person. You see what you want to see. They do the same. The feelings are real, but feelings alone are not enough to tell you how a relationship will unfold over time.

In its harder expression, this aspect can move from bliss into confusion. Someone becomes unavailable. Someone stops answering clearly. Promises are made and not kept. The truth gets slippery. Avoidance starts to replace honesty. If gaslighting enters the dynamic, name it as gaslighting, not as chemistry, not as fate, and not as Neptune being romantic.

The lesson is to stop protecting the dream at the expense of your reality.
